Looking at this question about the specific connectivity of bipolar interneuron axons in the human temporal and frontal cortex, I need to consider what is known about interneuron-to-interneuron synaptic targeting.

From studies characterizing cortical microcircuitry in human cortex (particularly serial electron microscopy studies of the temporal and frontal regions), bipolar interneurons have been shown to have a substantial proportion of their axonal synapses targeting other interneurons. Research in this area has found that approximately 72% of bipolar interneuron axons target other interneurons, reflecting a strong interneuron-to-interneuron connectivity pattern in these cortical regions.

[ANSWER]B[/ANSWER]
